mainTopic: Sources for the rule that liquids from forbidden or holy foods are like the food itself, and the argument over דון מינה ומינה versus דון מינה ואוקי באתרה
overview: The גמרא has shown that the Torah teaches separately that the juices or melted forms of שרצים, חלב, חמץ and נבלת עוף are forbidden. It asks why the Torah did not write this once, by שרצים. The answer is that שרצים are stricter, since even a tiny amount makes things טמא. Next it asks for the source of a ברייתא: liquids from טבל, חדש, הקדש, שביעית and כלאים are forbidden like the food itself. Most of these can be learned from the earlier cases, because they become forbidden on their own. הקדש is different, because a person makes it holy. The גמרא tries ביכורים, then תרומה, then both together, and rejects each one. It finally learns הקדש from תרומה or ביכורים paired with one of the earlier cases. Then it explains a משנה where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about juices of תרומה fruit. The argument depends on whether a comparison copies every detail (דון מינה ומינה) or only the basic rule (דון מינה ואוקי באתרה). Two more משניות that limit liquids to wine and oil, for ביכורים and for ערלה, are shown to follow רבי יהושע. The explanation of the ערלה case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not write the rule only by creeping animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the Torah could have written the liquid rule only by שרצים, and the other cases could be learned from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write the rule about creeping animals, and let these other cases come and be learned from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that each case needs its own separate source in the Torah. It suggests that one source, by שרצים, should have been enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, separate sources were brought for the liquids of שרצים, חלב, חמץ and נבלת עוף. The Torah does not waste words. So if one case could teach all the others, the extra sources would seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the Merciful One'; a name for ה׳, used when speaking about what the Torah wrote
Creeping creatures, like rodents and lizards, which are forbidden to eat and can make things טמא
And let them learn from it, meaning derive the other cases from this one

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write it by creeping creatures,
and let these others come and learn from them!
phrases.notes: 'These others' are the cases just discussed: melted חלב, dissolved חמץ and melted נבלת עוף.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּשְׁרָצִים, וְלֵיתוֹ הָנָךְ וְלִיגְמְרוּ מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier sugya's claim that each liquid prohibition needs its own source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for separate sources for the liquids of חלב, חמץ and נבלת עוף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah does not write extra words. If one case (שרצים) could teach the rest, the separate sources are unnecessary.

steps.title: Creeping creatures are stricter, so we cannot learn from them
steps.stepSummary: The other cases cannot be learned from שרצים, because שרצים make things טמא even in a tiny amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the comparison can be challenged: what is special about creeping creatures? They are special because their impurity works with even a tiny amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that learning from שרצים would not work, because שרצים have a special strictness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only learn a rule from one case to another if the first case is not stricter. שרצים make things טמא in a very small amount, unlike other foods whose rules start at a larger size. So maybe the liquid rule applies only to something that strict, and each other case needed its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a way to refute it; the comparison can be broken
What is special about X? It is that... (the standard way to point out a strictness that blocks a comparison)
Ritual impurity
In any tiny amount

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basic rule of learning one case from another: if the source case has a strictness the new case lacks, the comparison fails.

phrases.english: Because one can refute it:
What is special about creeping creatures? That their impurity is in any small amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: פירכא — showing that the source case has a special strictness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One source by שרצים could teach the liquid rule for all forbidden foods.
steps.terutzMaskana: שרצים are stricter (טמא in a tiny amount), so the other cases need their own sources.

steps.title: Where do we learn that liquids of טבל and similar foods are forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: liquids coming from טבל, חדש, הקדש, שביעית and כלאים are forbidden like the food itself. It asks where we learn this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that which was taught: untithed produce, the new grain, consecrated items, Sabbatical-year produce and forbidden mixtures — the liquids that come out of all of them are like the food itself. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question on the same theme. It quotes a ברייתא and asks for the Torah source behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These five foods are forbidden for different reasons, but no special verse was brought for their liquids. So the גמרא needs to find where the ברייתא gets its rule that the juice is forbidden just like the food.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been taken
New grain, forbidden until the עומר is brought
Something set aside as holy, for the בית המקדש
Produce of the seventh, שמיטה, year
Forbidden mixtures, like grain sown in a vineyard
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And that which is taught:
Untithed produce, and the new grain, and consecrated items,
and Sabbatical-year produce, and forbidden mixtures —
for all of them, the liquids that come out of them are like them.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier cases to a new list of foods, asking for their source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that liquids from טבל, חדש, הקדש, שביעית and כלאים are forbidden like the foods themselves.

steps.title: We cannot learn it from the earlier cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules out learning the ברייתא's rule from שרצים, חלב, חמץ and נבלה. Those are each an איסור הבא מאליו, a prohibition that comes about on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: let us learn from those earlier cases? What is special about them? They are prohibitions that come about on their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects an easy answer to its question and rejects it right away. This prepares the way for a different source in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obvious idea is to learn from the earlier cases. But each of those forbidden foods becomes forbidden by itself, without a person doing anything, which makes them a stricter kind of prohibition. So we cannot learn from them for a food in the ברייתא that lacks this strictness. Step 5 shows which case that is: הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say; the גמרא suggests a possible answer in order to answer it
A prohibition that comes about on its own, without a person causing it

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not answer the question 'מנלן'. It only blocks one possible answer; the real source comes later.

phrases.english: And if you would say: let us learn from these?
phrases.notes: 'These' means the earlier cases: שרצים, חלב, חמץ and נבלת עוף.

phrases.english: What is special about these?
That they are a prohibition that comes on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the obvious answer to the question of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion to learn the ברייתא's cases from שרצים, חלב, חמץ and נבלה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The earlier cases are each an איסור הבא מאליו, a stricter kind of prohibition. A food in the ברייתא whose prohibition does not come on its own (הקדש) does not share it.

steps.title: What about a prohibition a person creates?
steps.stepSummary: The earlier sources work for cases where the איסור comes on its own. For a case where it does not, like הקדש, we still need a source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, for cases where the prohibition comes about on its own we have a source. But where the prohibition does not come about on its own, how do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא grants that some of the ברייתא's cases can be learned from earlier sources. It then asks for a source for the one case that is different: הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, שרצים, חלב, חמץ and נבלה were set aside as sources because each is an איסור הבא מאליו. The cases in the ברייתא that are also like that can be learned from them. But הקדש becomes forbidden only when a person declares it holy, so it needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well. This grants one part before raising a problem with another part.
A prohibition that comes about on its own, without a person doing anything
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: It works out well where the prohibition comes about on its own,
phrases.notes: These are cases from the ברייתא like טבל, חדש, שביעית and כלאים, which become forbidden without anyone doing anything.

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּלָאו אִיסּוּר הַבָּא מֵאֵלָיו – מְנָלַן?
phrases.english: but where it is not a prohibition that comes about on its own, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: This means הקדש. It is forbidden only because a person made it holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the דחיה in Step 4. It accepts the sources for some cases and narrows the question to the remaining case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that liquid from a food whose איסור was created by a person (הקדש) is forbidden like the food.

steps.title: We learn it from ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes ביכורים as the source, since ביכורים are also forbidden only because a person sets them aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from ביכורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5. It says the source is ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביכורים are like הקדש because their איסור does not come on its own; the owner has to set them aside. If the liquid of ביכורים counts like the fruit, the same should be true for הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn it from, meaning we derive one case from another
The first fruits, which the owner brings to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: We learn it from first fruits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule for הקדש is learned from ביכורים, another case whose איסור comes from a person's action.

steps.title: How do we know this about ביכורים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that the liquid of ביכורים is treated like the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for ביכורים themselves, how do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: Before the גמרא can learn from ביכורים, it asks how we know the rule applies to ביכורים in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only learn from a case if the rule is already proven there. So the גמרא now needs a source showing that liquid from ביכורים has the same status as the fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: Themselves, meaning the case itself

phrases.english: And first fruits themselves, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the base of the source given in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that liquid of ביכורים has the status of ביכורים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: ביכורים can be brought as pressed grapes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי teaches that the word "פרי" means you normally bring fruit and not liquid. But the word "תביא" teaches that grapes that were pressed still count.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוסי teaches: "Fruit" means you bring fruit, not liquid. If someone brought grapes and pressed them, how do we know it counts? The פסוק says "you shall bring."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 7 with a teaching of רבי יוסי. It shows that the juice of ביכורים grapes still counts as ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "פרי" seems to exclude liquid. But the extra word "תביא" includes grapes that were pressed into wine. So the liquid of ביכורים carries the status of ביכורים, and this is the base the גמרא wanted for learning הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit, the word in the פסוק about ביכורים
A liquid or drink
He pressed them, meaning he trod grapes into juice
The פסוק teaches, used to bring a source from a word in the Torah

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yosei teaches:
"Fruit": you bring fruit,
phrases.notes: דברים 26:2

phrases.english: and you do not bring liquid.
If he brought grapes and pressed them, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know this still counts as bringing ביכורים?

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "You shall bring."
phrases.notes: This is from the same פסוק. The extra word includes grapes that were pressed into juice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Based on "תביא", pressed grapes still count as ביכורים. So their liquid has the status of ביכורים.

steps.title: ביכורים are too special to learn from
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא refutes learning הקדש from ביכורים, because ביכורים require a reading and being placed in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This can be refuted: what about ביכורים? They are special because they require a reading and being placed down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the source it just built. ביכורים have special features, so we cannot learn הקדש from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To learn one case from another, the two cases must be alike. ביכורים are stricter in a way: they need the reading of a special passage and they must be placed in the מקדש. Maybe that extra importance is why their liquid counts, and הקדש lacks it. So the question from Step 5 is open again.

keyTerms.meaning: One can refute this, by pointing out a difference between the cases
What about this case, since it has a special feature? This is how a refutation is worded.
Reading, here the passage said when bringing ביכורים
Placing the ביכורים down in the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the rule about liquid of הקדש is wrong. The גמרא is only saying that ביכורים cannot be its source, so it still needs another one.

phrases.english: One can refute this:
What about first fruits?
They are special because they require reading and placing!
phrases.notes: The reading is the passage "ארמי אובד אבי" (דברים 26:5).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the source proposed in Step 6 and backed up in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the הקדש rule from ביכורים. It does not deny the rule about ביכורים itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ביכורים have special features (קריאה and הנחה) that הקדש lacks, so the cases are not alike.

steps.title: A new try: learn from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: Since ביכורים did not work, the גמרא proposes learning the rule for הקדש from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops ביכורים as the source and suggests תרומה instead. This opens a new attempt that the next lines will test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is still to show that liquid from הקדש fruit is forbidden like the fruit. תרומה is a good candidate because, like הקדש, it becomes forbidden only when a person sets it aside. Also, תרומה does not need a reading or placing in the מקדש, which was the weakness of ביכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the גמרא is switching to a new approach.
Learns or derives one law from another.
The portion of produce given to a כהן, forbidden to non-כהנים.

phrases.english: Rather, he learns it from תרומה.
phrases.notes: He means: learn the rule about liquid from הקדש fruit from the rule about liquid from תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source from ביכורים, which step 9 rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תרומה is offered as the source for the rule about הקדש liquid.

steps.title: Where does תרומה itself get this rule?
steps.stepSummary: Before using תרומה as a source, the גמרא asks how we know that liquid from תרומה is forbidden like the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for תרומה itself, how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check the new source. You cannot learn from תרומה unless you first know that תרומה has this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A source is only useful if its own rule is established. So the גמרא asks where we learn that liquid squeezed from תרומה counts as תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Itself.
From where do we know? It asks for a source.

phrases.english: And תרומה itself, from where do we know it?
phrases.notes: From where do we know that liquid from תרומה is forbidden just like the fruit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the basis of the source proposed in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that liquid from תרומה is treated like the תרומה fruit.

steps.title: תרומה is compared to ביכורים in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: תרומה gets the rule from ביכורים, because the Torah calls ביכורים "תרומת ידך," which links the two.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is compared to ביכורים, because the Master said that "the תרומה of your hand" means ביכורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that תרומה is linked to ביכורים through a פסוק. So whatever is true of ביכורים liquid is also true of תרומה liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls ביכורים by the name "תרומה." That creates a הקש: the two are compared. Step 8 already showed that pressed ביכורים grapes still count, so liquid from תרומה counts too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was compared through a הֶקֵּשׁ, a link the Torah makes between two topics so they share laws.
"The offering of your hand." A phrase from the פסוק that is read as meaning ביכורים.
First fruits brought to the מקדש.

phrases.english: Because it is compared to ביכורים,
as the Master said: "And the offering of your hand"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:17

phrases.english: these are ביכורים.
phrases.notes: Since the Torah calls ביכורים "תרומה," the two share the rule that their liquid counts like the fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by linking תרומה to ביכורים, whose liquid rule was shown in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הקש from the phrase "ותרומת ידך," which refers to ביכורים, gives תרומה the same liquid rule as ביכורים.

steps.title: תרומה is stricter: it carries death and a fifth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning הקדש from תרומה, because eating תרומה carries מיתה and חומש, which make it stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about תרומה? It is special because one is liable for it to death and to a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from תרומה. It points out that תרומה is stricter than הקדש, so its rules may not carry over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-כהן who eats תרומה can be punished with death and must pay back an extra fifth. Because תרומה is so strict, maybe that is why even its liquid is forbidden. הקדש is not that strict, so we cannot assume the same for it.

keyTerms.meaning: "What about X? It has a special feature." A standard way to show a source is stricter and cannot be learned from.
Death at the hands of Heaven, the punishment for a non-כהן who eats תרומה on purpose.
An extra fifth added when paying back for eating תרומה by mistake.

phrases.english: What about תרומה?
It is special, since one is liable for it to death and a fifth.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִתְרוּמָה, שֶׁכֵּן חַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ מִיתָה וָחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source from תרומה proposed in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from תרומה alone to הקדש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תרומה has strict punishments, מיתה and חומש, that הקדש does not have, so its liquid rule may come from that strictness.

steps.title: Try learning from both together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning הקדש from תרומה and ביכורים together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from both of them, from תרומה and ביכורים.
steps.whatsHappening: Since each source failed alone, the גמרא tries combining them. The next step will test this combined source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ביכורים was rejected because of the reading and the placing in the מקדש, which תרומה does not need. תרומה was rejected because of מיתה and חומש. The hope is that one source covers the weakness of the other, so together they prove the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From both of them.

phrases.english: Rather, he learns it from both of them,
from תרומה and ביכורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both single sources were rejected in steps 9 and 13, it combines them.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learn הקדש from תרומה and ביכורים together.

steps.title: Both share the same strictness
steps.stepSummary: The combined proof fails, because both תרומה and ביכורים carry מיתה together with חומש, a combination הקדש does not have (הקדש has חומש but no מיתה).
steps.simpleTranslation: What about תרומה and ביכורים? They are special because one is liable for them to death and a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the combined proof. Both sources share the same strict feature, so together they still cannot teach about הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Combining two sources works only if they do not share a strictness that the new case lacks. Here, both תרומה and ביכורים carry מיתה together with חומש, while הקדש has no מיתה. So their liquid rule may come from that shared strictness, and the search for a source for הקדש goes on.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable, meaning one gets a punishment or must pay.
Property set aside for the מקדש. This is the case we are trying to find a source for.

steps.whatToRemember: Neither תרומה, nor ביכורים, nor both together can teach the liquid rule for הקדש. ביכורים needs a reading and the מקדש, and both carry מיתה together with חומש, a combination הקדש lacks.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that combining two sources always works. It fails here because the strict feature, מיתה and חומש, is found in both of them, so neither one covers for the other.

phrases.english: What about תרומה and ביכורים?
They are special, since one is liable for them to death and a fifth!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִתְרוּמָה וּבִכּוּרִים, שֶׁכֵּן חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶם מִיתָה וָחוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the combined source proposed in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from תרומה and ביכורים together to הקדש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources share the strictness of מיתה and חומש, which הקדש lacks.

steps.title: The final source: תרומה or ביכורים plus one earlier case
steps.stepSummary: Since תרומה and ביכורים together failed, the גמרא instead pairs one of them with one of the earlier cases to teach that liquid from הקדש is like the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the rule for הקדש is learned from תרומה together with one of those earlier cases, or from ביכורים together with one of those earlier cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its working answer. It learns the rule for הקדש from a new pair: תרומה or ביכורים, together with one of the earlier cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 rejected תרומה plus ביכורים, because both carry מיתה and חומש and הקדש does not. Here each pair joins a case that has מיתה and חומש with an earlier case that does not. So that strictness is no longer shared by the whole source, and the proof can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (it is learned) from
One of those (earlier cases)
The portion of produce given to a כהן
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that liquid from הקדש counts like the fruit is learned from a pair: תרומה or ביכורים, plus one of the earlier cases.

phrases.english: Rather, it is learned from תרומה
phrases.notes: "It" means the rule that liquid coming out of הקדש fruit is treated like the fruit itself.

phrases.english: and one of those,
phrases.notes: "Those" are the earlier cases the גמרא already tried, like a melted bird נבלה or dissolved חמץ.

phrases.english: or from ביכורים and one of those.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed pairing from step 15 with a new pairing that avoids the shared strictness.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Learn הקדש from תרומה plus one earlier case, or from ביכורים plus one earlier case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Liquid from הקדש is forbidden like the fruit, learned from a mixed pair of sources.

steps.title: A משנה: juices of תרומה fruit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי אליעזר says a non-כהן who drank fruit juices of תרומה pays קרן וחומש, and רבי יהושע says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: date honey, apple wine, vinegar from late-season grapes, and other fruit juices of תרומה: רבי אליעזר obligates the principal and a fifth, and רבי יהושע exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic connected to the comparison between תרומה and ביכורים. It quotes a משנה about someone who drank juices from תרומה fruit, setting up the question of what the argument depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating real תרומה by mistake means paying back its value plus an extra fifth. The question here is whether juices from fruits like dates and apples count as תרומה for this penalty. רבי אליעזר says yes, and רבי יהושע says no.

keyTerms.meaning: Paying back the value plus an extra fifth, the penalty for a non-כהן who eats תרומה by mistake
Obligates (says he must pay)
Exempts (says he does not have to pay)
Small late-season grapes, not good for making wine

phrases.english: And that which we learned in a משנה:
date honey, and apple wine,
and vinegar from late-season grapes,
and other kinds of fruit of תרומה –
phrases.notes: He means juices made from these fruits, which a non-כהן drank.

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר obligates the principal and a fifth,
and רבי יהושע exempts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source for הקדש to a related משנה about liquids of תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: juices of תרומה fruit carry קרן וחומש; רבי יהושע: they do not.

steps.title: The root of the argument: how far a comparison reaches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the argument depends on and answers that they disagree about דון מינה ומינה versus דון מינה ואוקי באתרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they argue? They argue about 'learn from it, and again from it' versus 'learn from it, but leave it in its own place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind the argument in the משנה. It answers that the two sages disagree about how much we copy when we learn one case from another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דון מינה ומינה means that when we learn case B from case A, we copy all of A's details into B. דון מינה ואוקי באתרה means we copy only the basic rule, and B keeps its own details. The argument about juices of תרומה depends on which method we use.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they argue?
Learn from it, and again from it: copy all the details of the source case
Learn from it, but leave it in its place: copy only the basic rule, keep the new case's own details
They argue

steps.confusionAlert: Both sages agree that something is learned from ביכורים. The argument is only about how much gets copied over.

phrases.english: About what do they argue?
About 'learn from it, and again from it,'
and 'learn from it, but leave it in its place' they argue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the argument quoted in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע depends on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue whether a comparison copies all details (דון מינה ומינה) or only the basic rule (דון מינה ואוקי באתרה).
steps.whyThisMatters: These two methods of learning one case from another come up in other places too, so this step teaches a basic tool of the גמרא.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's view: copy everything from ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns from ביכורים both that liquid is like the fruit and that this applies even to other kinds of fruit, so all juices of תרומה count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds 'learn from it, and again from it.' Just as liquid from ביכורים is like the fruit, so too liquid from תרומה is like the fruit. And again: just as ביכורים includes even other kinds of fruit, so too תרומה includes even other kinds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אליעזר's side. He learns two things from ביכורים, so juices of any תרומה fruit count as תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First lesson: liquid from ביכורים is like the fruit, so liquid from תרומה is too. Second lesson: ביכורים applies to other kinds of fruit, not only grapes and olives, so the liquid rule for תרומה also covers other fruits. That is why he says a person who drank date honey or apple wine of תרומה pays קרן וחומש.

keyTerms.meaning: The liquid that comes out of them
Like them (has the same status as the fruit)
Other kinds (of fruit)
Just as... so too: the form of a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר copies both details from ביכורים: liquid counts like the fruit, and this covers all kinds of fruit. So juices of any תרומה fruit carry קרן וחומש.

phrases.english: For רבי אליעזר holds:
learn from it, and again from it,
just as with ביכורים –
the liquid that comes out of them is like them,
so too with תרומה –
the liquid that comes out of them is like them,
and again from it –
phrases.notes: This is the second lesson he copies from ביכורים.

phrases.english: just as ביכורים includes even other kinds,
phrases.notes: Other kinds besides grapes and olives, the fruits usually squeezed into wine and oil.

phrases.aramaic: אַף תְּרוּמָה נָמֵי אֲפִילּוּ שְׁאָר מִינִין.
phrases.english: so too תרומה includes even other kinds.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: דּוּן מִינַּהּ וּמִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the method of דון מינה ומינה from step 18 to explain רבי אליעזר's ruling in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר copies from ביכורים both that liquid counts like the fruit and that this covers all kinds, so juices of any תרומה fruit carry קרן וחומש.

steps.title: רבי יהושע learns from ביכורים but keeps the rule limited to wine and oil
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע uses דון מינה ואוקי באתרה. He learns from ביכורים that juice of תרומה is like the fruit, but only wine and oil, because only those liquids are named for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע holds: learn from it. Just as with ביכורים the juice that comes out of them is like them, so too with תרומה the juice that comes out of it is like it. But leave it in its own place: just as with the liquids that are holy as תרומה, wine and oil count and nothing else does, so too with juice that comes out of תרומה, wine and oil count and nothing else does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהושע exempts a non-כהן who drank fruit juices of תרומה. He takes only the basic idea from ביכורים and then follows the rules of תרומה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From ביכורים he takes only the idea that 'juice is like the fruit.' He does not take ביכורים's details. Since the liquids of תרומה are only wine and oil, only juice from grapes and olives counts like the fruit, so other fruit juices are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn the main idea from the other case, but apply it with the details of the case's own place.
Liquids that come out of them (juice squeezed from the fruit).
Like them, with the same holy status as the fruit.
Wine and oil.
Anything else.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר learns the whole rule from ביכורים (דון מינה ומינה), so all fruit juices count. רבי יהושע learns only the idea and keeps תרומה's limits (דון מינה ואוקי באתרה), so only wine and oil count.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע does agree that juice of תרומה can be like the fruit. He only limits it to wine and oil. That is why he exempts the other juices in the משנה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua holds: learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: מָה בִּכּוּרִים – מַשְׁקִין הַיּוֹצְאִין מֵהֶן כְּמוֹתָן,
phrases.english: just as with first fruits, the liquids that come out of them are like them,

phrases.aramaic: אַף תְּרוּמָה – מַשְׁקִין הַיּוֹצְאִין מֵהֶן כְּמוֹתָן.
phrases.english: so too with terumah, the liquids that come out of it are like it.
But leave it in its own place:
just as with liquids that are holy as terumah,
phrases.notes: The פסוק about giving תרומה names only wine and oil (דברים 18:4).

phrases.aramaic: תִּירוֹשׁ וְיִצְהָר – אִין, מִידֵּי אַחֲרִינָא – לָא,
phrases.english: wine and oil, yes; anything else, no,
so too, for liquids that come out of them to be like them,

phrases.aramaic: תִּירוֹשׁ וְיִצְהָר – אִין, מִידֵּי אַחֲרִינָא – לָא.
phrases.english: wine and oil, yes; anything else, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation started in step 18. Step 19 gave רבי אליעזר's reasoning, and this step gives רבי יהושע's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע learns from ביכורים that juice is like the fruit, but limits it to wine and oil, following תרומה's own rules. So he exempts other fruit juices.

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה that ביכורים juice is only from olives and grapes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that only olive oil and grape wine may be brought as ביכורים in liquid form, and asks which תנא it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that which we learned in a משנה: one may not bring ביכורים as a liquid except what comes out of olives and grapes. Whose view is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an unnamed משנה and asks whose opinion it matches. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה limits liquid ביכורים to wine and oil. That limit sounds like רבי יהושע's approach, not רבי אליעזר's, who treats all fruit juices like the fruit. The גמרא asks in order to tie the משנה to one side of the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose (opinion) is it? Asked about an unnamed source.
Bring (to the בית המקדש).
Olives (the source of oil).
Grapes (the source of wine).

phrases.english: And that which we learned in a mishnah:
one may not bring first fruits as a liquid

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַזֵּיתִים וּמִן הָעֲנָבִים –
phrases.english: except what comes out of olives and grapes —
whose view is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two methods just explained to figure out which side an unnamed משנה follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the משנה follows when it limits liquid ביכורים to wine and oil.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהושע, who learns ביכורים back from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יהושע. Using דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, he learns ביכורים from תרומה, so ביכורים liquids are also limited to wine and oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the view of רבי יהושע, who says: learn from it, but leave it in its own place. And he learns ביכורים from תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is רבי יהושע's view. He also learns back in the other direction, from תרומה to ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע already limited תרומה juice to wine and oil. Now we see he also applies that limit back to ביכורים, so only wine and oil from ביכורים count as liquid ביכורים. For רבי אליעזר, other fruit juices would also count, so the משנה cannot be his.

keyTerms.meaning: And he learns them, deriving one law from another.
From תרומה.

steps.confusionAlert: The learning goes both ways here. ביכורים teaches תרומה that juice is like the fruit, and תרומה teaches ביכורים that this only applies to wine and oil.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehoshua, who says:
learn from it, but leave it in its own place,
and he learns first fruits from terumah.
phrases.notes: He means that ביכורים take on תרומה's limit, so only wine and oil count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהושע. He learns ביכורים from תרומה, limiting liquid ביכורים to wine and oil.

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה that lashes for ערלה juice apply only to olives and grapes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that one gets forty lashes for drinking ערלה juice only if it came from olives or grapes, and asks whose view it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that which we learned in a משנה: one does not get the forty lashes because of ערלה except for what comes out of olives and grapes. Whose view is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same 'whose view?' question about another משנה, this time about ערלה. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the ביכורים משנה, this one treats only wine and oil like the forbidden fruit. The גמרא wants to know which תנא's approach supports this limit for ערלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Receive the forty lashes (מלקות) as punishment.
Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden.

phrases.english: And that which we learned in a mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין סוֹפְגִין אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים מִשּׁוּם עׇרְלָה,
phrases.english: one does not receive the forty lashes because of orlah,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַזֵּיתִים וּמִן הָעֲנָבִים –
phrases.english: except for what comes out of olives and grapes —
whose view is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דִּתְנַן: אֵין סוֹפְגִין אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים מִשּׁוּם עׇרְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question as step 21, now about a ערלה ruling from the same משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the משנה follows when it limits lashes for ערלה juice to wine and oil.

steps.title: The ערלה ruling follows רבי יהושע, starting with ביכורים learned from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה about ערלה juice follows רבי יהושע. He holds דון מינה ואוקי באתרה and learns ביכורים from תרומה, so only wine and oil count as the fruit. This is the first link in a chain that will lead to ערלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is the view of רבי יהושע, who said: learn from it, but set the rule in its own place. And he learns ביכורים from תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 23: the ערלה משנה follows רבי יהושע. It begins explaining his chain of learning, and the next link, which connects ערלה, is still coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 22 the גמרא used this same reasoning to explain why only wine and oil count for ביכורים. Here it repeats that reasoning because ערלה needs to borrow the limited ביכורים rule. Since ביכורים was itself limited by learning from תרומה, any law that learns from ביכורים will also be limited to olives and grapes.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden to eat or drink
Learn the basic rule from the source, but keep the details of the case you are learning about
And he learns or derives one law from another
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is just repeating Step 22 for no reason. The question now is about ערלה, and the ביכורים link is being set up so that ערלה can learn from it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one limitation can pass down a chain. A rule learned from תרומה, where only wine and oil are mentioned, carries that same limit to every law that learns from it.

phrases.english: It is the view of Rabbi Yehoshua,
phrases.notes: "It" means the משנה from Step 23 about forty lashes for ערלה juice.

phrases.english: who said: Learn from it, but set it in its own place,
and he derives first fruits from teruma,
phrases.notes: So for ביכורים too, only wine and oil count like the fruit itself, just as with תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא, דְּאָמַר: דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְּאַתְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23 by identifying רבי יהושע, and reuses the ביכורים-from-תרומה derivation from Step 22 as the first link toward ערלה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose view is the משנה that limits lashes for ערלה liquid to olives and grapes?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It follows רבי יהושע, who uses דון מינה ואוקי באתרה. He learns ביכורים from תרומה, which limits ביכורים to wine and oil. This starts a chain that will carry the same limit to ערלה.
